**Section C: Comprehension (10 marks)**

Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow it, and as far as possible, in your own words.

**Pills that Kill**

Drugs are double-edged swords: they heal as well as kill, depending on how they are used. In most rural areas of Cameroon today, more and more people are resorting to auto-medication because civil servants, eager to improve their financial situation, and young unemployed people are opening patent drugstores or parading through villages with baskets full of pills. Very few users, educated or not, stop to ask themselves whether the pills they are buying and consuming are appropriate for the illness they are suffering from, or if the pills are being taken properly and in the required dosage.

A couple of years ago, a lady, Miss A, offered a friend, Mrs B, a bottle of beer. Mrs B had just bought three capsules of Flagyl which she swallowed down with the beer. Hours later at home, she started vomiting. Suspecting that she had been poisoned, she told her relatives what had happened before being rushed to the hospital.

At the hospital, Mrs B told the doctor what she had taken earlier that day. Realising her error, the doctor explained to her that beer and Flagyl do not mix at all. It was the reaction that had caused the vomiting. An antidote was prescribed and Mrs B was taken home. When she got home, her jubilant relatives had just returned from Miss A's house where they had smashed and destroyed her property, only to be told that the vomiting was due to drug reaction. A long-lasting friendship was thus ruined simply because of ignorance.

Situations like this occur frequently in our towns and villages, where everybody plays the role of a medical doctor. People are dying in large numbers, but we fail to acknowledge that medical drug abuse can be one of the major reasons. Drugs that have been banned from circulating in the country still find their way into distribution systems and finally into stores where managers possess very little or no information on how dangerous these substances can be to the human body. It is thus very dangerous to swallow pills that have not been prescribed by a competent health care worker or drug specialist.

Most of the drugs that circulate in rural areas and big towns through street hawkers come from illegal sources and are not usually kept under the right conditions. Some are fake drugs that contain harmful elements. But pharmacists also confirm that they have seen instances where capsules contain nothing but ordinary corn or cassava flour. The pharmacists insist that the trade marks or the countries of origin are not guarantees of the quality because these can be pirated and fake drugs packaged.

In Bamenda, efforts to prosecute the patent medicine stores ended with a court case that was quickly dismissed because the patent medicine store owners pay taxes into the national coffer. This continuous war between the pharmacists and the illegal operators is not just a capitalist duel of sales and profits. It is a battle between experts and charlatans, between right and wrong. In a nutshell, it is a matter of life and death. The serious consequences of this kind of drug abuse should never be taken lightly!

*(Adapted from an article by Omer Songwe in the August 1999 issue of The Farmer's Voice)*

**Comprehension questions (10 marks)**

1. According to the passage, which of these statements is true? Mark an (X) in front of the correct statement; then justify your choice. (2 marks)

   a) Competent health care workers often prescribe harmful drugs.
   b) The problem of patent drugstores is aggravated by corruption.
   c) Government should not ban any drugs.
   d) If a medicine has a well-known trade mark, you can be sure it is authentic.

   Justification

2. Why is it dangerous for people to buy medicine in a patent drugstore or from a hawker? Give at least two reasons. (2 marks)

3. Why did Mrs B get sick? (1 mark)

4. Why did Mrs B's relatives destroy Miss A's property? (1 mark)

5. What health problems can be caused by drug abuse? (2 marks)

6. According to the passage, are all fake drugs harmful? Explain. (2 marks)

**Question concernée : n°1 (2 marks).**

### Rappel de méthode
Une question de compréhension se répond en reformulant un passage précis du texte, avec ses propres mots autant que possible. Pour une question à choix (« mark an X »), il faut ensuite justifier ce choix par un fait explicitement présent dans le texte, pas par une simple reformulation de l'énoncé de la réponse choisie.

**Réponse : (X) b) The problem of patent drugstores is aggravated by corruption.**

**Justification :** Le texte rapporte qu'à Bamenda, les poursuites judiciaires contre les vendeurs de médicaments en pharmacie de rue ont été rapidement abandonnées simplement parce que ces vendeurs paient des impôts à l'État (« because the patent medicine store owners pay taxes into the national coffer »). Cela montre que des considérations financières, et non le respect de la loi, déterminent qui est poursuivi ou non, ce qui aggrave concrètement le problème plutôt que de le résoudre.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Non, tous les faux médicaments ne sont pas nocifs au sens strict : le texte précise que les pharmaciens ont découvert des capsules ne contenant que de la farine de maïs ou de manioc ordinaire, sans substance dangereuse. Cependant, d'autres faux médicaments contiennent bel et bien des éléments nocifs. Dans tous les cas, ces faux médicaments restent dangereux indirectement, car ils laissent la vraie maladie du patient sans traitement efficace, ce qui peut aggraver son état même sans intoxication directe.

### Piège à éviter
Répondre simplement « oui » ou « non » à cette question fait perdre des points : le texte distingue explicitement deux catégories de faux médicaments (ceux qui sont inertes, comme la farine de manioc, et ceux qui contiennent des éléments nocifs), et une bonne réponse doit refléter cette nuance.

### Conseil
Quand une question de compréhension commence par « Are all... » ou « Is it always... », méfie-toi d'une réponse binaire trop simple : le texte source nuance presque toujours ce type d'affirmation générale, et le correcteur attend que cette nuance apparaisse dans la réponse.

Ces deux questions ont été renumérotées ici 3 et 4 par cohérence avec le barème total de 10 points.
